# Editor's review pack

For Dr Kunda Shahane, editor-in-chief. Everything that needs her decision or signature is in this one document.
Each claim appears once, even if several units use it. Claims she has already verified are not repeated.
Claims that a second AI has not yet confirmed against the source are held back, so that she checks each fact only once.

**4 decision(s). 5 claim(s) to approve again. 39 new claim(s) to check. 112 claim(s) held back until cross-checked.**

## Part A. Decisions

**Q1. ASE guideline, pulsed-wave Doppler of the aortic arch and isthmus. The text (p. 689) includes 'arches' in the minimum assessment; Table 6 (p. 693) marks the transverse arch and isthmus optional and separately requires the distal ductus arteriosus. ChatGPT's check of the PDF confirmed that the guideline does not reconcile the two. How should the course teach it?**

- [ ] Teach as optional (as in Table 6)
- [ ] Teach as required (as in the text)
- [ ] Keep the present wording: state both, teach neither as the rule

If no answer: Present wording stays: units F1 and XA5 state the disagreement and teach neither reading as the rule.
Affects: Units F1 and XA5

**Q2. After a normal early (11 to 14 week) heart check, may unit D9 say plainly that the full second-trimester cardiac screen is still required? The ASE guideline says this for early fetal echocardiography (repeat at 18 to 20 weeks); the ISUOG screening guideline does not say it in so many words.**

- [ ] Yes, say it plainly for screening as the editor's teaching
- [ ] No, keep it as the ASE statement about echocardiography only

If no answer: D9 quotes the ASE statement under its own heading and makes no rule for screening.
Affects: Unit D9

**Q3. Rate thresholds. ISUOG (screening): refer for a persistent rate of 110 or less, or 180 or more. ASE (echocardiography): a sustained rate below 120, or above 160 to 180, is abnormal. Units D8 and F2 teach the ISUOG thresholds for the screener and mention the ASE wording. Is that right for this course?**

- [ ] Yes
- [ ] No, teach this instead: ____________

If no answer: As drafted: ISUOG thresholds for the screener, ASE wording mentioned.
Affects: Units D8, D10, F2

**Q4. Does the consent held for archive cases cover publication for teaching in a paid product (not only clinical care)?**

- [ ] Yes, wording covers it
- [ ] No or unsure: re-consent or do not use
- [ ] Ask the legal advisor

If no answer: No archive clip is published until this is confirmed in writing.
Affects: All clip drills and the case atlas

Mark each: OK / change (write the correction) / remove.

### C1. To approve again

You approved these on 13 Nov in an earlier wording. A check against the guideline PDF found that each had lost a qualifier. The wording below restores it; the note says what changed.

| Claim | Statement | Where in source | Used in | OK / change / remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IS23-017 | Still frames and video clips of the recommended structures and views should be archived so that the examination can later be reviewed for adequacy, with appropriate patient identification in the clinical examination record, labelling of laterality and orientation where appropriate, and consideration of local or national archiving standards (good practice point). **Note:** Approved by the editor on 13 Nov 2026 in an earlier wording (Dr Kunda Shahane, 2026-11-13 (approved review sheet for v0.2 in full; approval relayed by the project owner)). Reworded after the cross-check found: Technical factors, Zoom, cine-loop and image storage, p. 789 also calls for appropriate patient identification in the clinical examination record and consideration of local or national archiving standards. Laterality and orientation labels alone do not cover its documentation instructions. Needs the editor's re-approval. | ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Technical factors: Zoom, cine-loop and image storage, p. 789 | D1, D2, D3, D5, D6, D13 | |
| IS23-036 | Transient bradycardia is seen in normal second-trimester fetuses and is associated with transducer pressure; persistent bradycardia (110 bpm or less) in a well fetus needs timely evaluation by a fetal cardiac specialist. Possible causes include frequent blocked atrial ectopic beats, atrioventricular block and sinus bradycardia. **Note:** Approved by the editor on 13 Nov 2026 in an earlier wording (Dr Kunda Shahane, 2026-11-13 (approved review sheet for v0.2 in full; approval relayed by the project owner)). Reworded after the cross-check found: Four-chamber view, p. 792 describes an association between transient bradycardia and probe pressure. “Often from” strengthens that association to a cause. The persistent rate threshold, well-fetus qualifier, referral and listed possible causes agree. Needs the editor's re-approval. | ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Four-chamber view, p. 792 | D1, D8, D10, F2 | |
| IS23-047 | Two separate atrioventricular valves should open separately and freely, with the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve inserting closer to the apex than the mitral valve (normal offset); abnormal alignment can be a key sonographic finding in anomalies such as atrioventricular septal defect. **Note:** Approved by the editor on 13 Nov 2026 in an earlier wording (Dr Kunda Shahane, 2026-11-13 (approved review sheet for v0.2 in full; approval relayed by the project owner)). Reworded after the cross-check found: Four-chamber view, p. 793 says abnormal AV valve alignment can be a key sonographic finding in anomalies such as AV septal defect. The claim makes it categorical. The normal offset and valve-opening descriptions agree. Needs the editor's re-approval. | ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Four-chamber view, p. 793; Table 1 | D1, D4, D13 | |
| IS23-063 | The axial appearances of the RVOT, branch pulmonary arteries and ductal and aortic arches form a continuum of views that varies with transducer orientation and fetal lie; assessment is likely to be more reliable live or on cine-loop than from still images alone. **Note:** Approved by the editor on 13 Nov 2026 in an earlier wording (Dr Kunda Shahane, 2026-11-13 (approved review sheet for v0.2 in full; approval relayed by the project owner)). Reworded after the cross-check found: RVOT view, 3VV and 3VTV, p. 794 describes greater reliability of live or cine review as likely. The claim states it without that qualification. Figure 8 on p. 795 illustrates the continuum. Needs the editor's re-approval. | ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: RVOT view, 3VV and 3VTV, p. 794; Figure 8, p. 795 | D1, D6, D13 | |
| IS23-077 | In routine second-trimester screening the colour velocity scale should be about 50-70 cm/s for intracardiac structures and vessels, and lower, about 15-25 cm/s, for venous structures. Low colour persistence is ordinarily built into cardiac presets. **Note:** Approved by the editor on 13 Nov 2026 in an earlier wording (Dr Kunda Shahane, 2026-11-13 (approved review sheet for v0.2 in full; approval relayed by the project owner)). Reworded after the cross-check found: Color flow Doppler ultrasound, p. 796 recommends the two stated velocity scales. It describes low colour persistence as ordinarily built into cardiac presets, without giving it the same direct instruction as the scale setting. Needs the editor's re-approval. | ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Color flow Doppler ultrasound, p. 796 | D1, D2, D7, F1 | |
